summary: Chlodwig H. Werba works in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the University of Vienna, attested from 1990 to 2006 as Prof. Dr. and again in 2022.
Chogye Shabdrung is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sakya College in 2003 under Khenchen Sonam Gyatso.

Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Chogye Trichen Rinpoche studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Kunga Chophel, Geshe Tsechok in 1929, and Zimwok Rinpoche. In 1928, he became the Eighteenth Chogye Trichen at Phenpo Nalendra Monastery.

Chogyū Takayama worked in philosophy, Japanology, and other fields. He studied at Fukushima Prefectural Asaka High School from around 1887 to 1890 and at the University of Tokyo from circa 1893 to 1896.
Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, whom he also taught.
Chong Go is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Dongguk University and studied under the traditional teacher Daehaeng (attested 2012).
Chris Clark works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Sydney by 2015 under doctoral supervisor Mark Allon, and was an honorary associate there in 2019.
Chris Williams is active in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Attested in 2026, he studied at the University of Bristol as an MPhil and PhD student under doctoral supervisor Rita Langer.

Christiaan Hooykaas was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his Ph.D. at Leiden University (1921–1929), studying under Jean Philippe Vogel in 1921, and held posts at the University of Indonesia (1946) and SOAS (1951–1953).

Christiaan Snouck Hurgronje studied at Leiden University (~1874–1880), under Theodor Nöldeke (~1880–1881), and at Nederlands-Indische Bestuursacademie. A religious studies scholar, he held posts at Leiden University (1887, 1889–1890, 1906–1927) and Oostersch Genootschap in Nederland (~1920–1921).

Christian August Brandis was a scholar of philosophy and history/archaeology. He studied at Kiel University (~1808–1812) and held academic posts at the University of Copenhagen (~1812–1815), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1816–1821), and the University of Bonn (~1821–1867).

Christian Bartholomae studied at Munich, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Leipzig (Ph.D. 1878). Working in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he held posts at Halle-Wittenberg, Münster (1885–1898), Giessen (1898–1909), Strasbourg (1909), and Heidelberg (1909–1924).

Christian Bernert specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the International Buddhist Academy and the University of Vienna, where he completed his Magister under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and also studied with Junjie Chu, Karin Preisendanz, and Gerald Hödl.

Christian Charles Josias von Bunsen studied at Marburg, Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne, Munich, Leiden, Copenhagen, and under Silvestre de Sacy. Working in linguistics, religious studies, and history/archaeology, he served as Prussian envoy (~1823–1854) and founded the German Archaeological Institute.

Christian Coseru studied at the University of Bucharest and completed his PhD at the Australian National University (~1999–2003). Active in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology, he joined the College of Charleston (~2006) and visited UC Berkeley (~2017).

Christian Ferstl specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna, where he held a lectorate in 2014, and worked as a research project collaborator at the University of Leipzig in 2021.

Christian Gilberti works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He has been affiliated with the University of California, Berkeley, serving in South and Southeast Asian Studies and attested as a student representative in 2026.

Christian Gottlob Heyne studied at the University of Leipzig (1748–1752). A scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology, he served as professor of eloquence and poetry at the University of Göttingen (from 1763) and director of its library (1764–1812).

Christian Haskett works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin–Madison (attested 2010), advised by Robert A. F. Thurman and Michael Chamberlain, and held a post at Washington and Lee University (attested 2010).

Christian K. Wedemeyer earned his MA and PhD at Columbia under Robert A. F. Thurman. Active in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology, he held posts at Columbia, Antioch, Copenhagen (2000–2003), and the University of Chicago (2003–2011).
